summary: The note traces the growth of the Riverside Running Marathon from a small community race founded by Robert "Bobby" Jameson into a large regional event with multiple distances, a Health and Wellness Fair, charitable giving, a corporate challenge and a cultural showcase. It highlights community involvement from the town council, local businesses and volunteers. The piece presents the marathon as a lasting tradition promoting health, unity and local pride. The note contains date inconsistencies (a 2023 edition, a 2024 first race, and later years through 2034).
one_line: The Riverside Running Marathon grew from a 150-runner local race into a major community event with a wellness fair, charity support and cultural showcase.
key_facts: The Riverside Running Marathon was founded by local fitness enthusiast Robert "Bobby" Jameson.
The first race looped through Riverside Park and drew about 150 participants; the note dates it to September 2024.
The note says the latest edition was scheduled for October 21, 2023, which conflicts with the stated 2024 start date.
Anderson's Sports Apparel and Green Bowl Bites, along with the town council, supported the marathon as it grew.
By its fifth iteration the event offered distances from a 5K fun run to the full 26.2-mile marathon.
The course passes landmarks such as Lakeview Park and historic downtown avenues.
The first Health and Wellness Fair began September 15, 2027, a week before the marathon, offering free seminars, fitness classes and nutrition advice.
A portion of entry fees goes to the Riverside Education Foundation and the Greenways Conservation Project.
A corporate challenge element was inaugurated in 2026 to encourage rivalries among local businesses.
Luis Hernández, a high school track athlete, earned scholarships based on his performances at the event.
Annette Kirby's dance group has performed at the marathon since 2029.
Sarah Leigh has been a volunteer coordinator since the early days of the marathon.
